subject: Task 26.3 attempt 2 - Guard enforcement rework (re-audit of F-26.3-TQ-01/02/03). Do the three recorded fixes genuinely close the prior findings, do the guards still discriminate and remain satisfiable, and were any new test-quality gaps introduced?
audit_method: Independent re-audit. No code, script, test, or documentation was modified. All mutations were performed on a throwaway copy at /tmp/final-review/test-quality/repo (docs/, scripts/, .opencode/, AGENTS.md, GOALS.md, PLANS.md, README.md copied from the working tree, with docs/implementation/26.3 set aside as /tmp/final-review/test-quality/263-aside). The real tree's `git status --short`, `git diff --name-only` and `git diff --numstat` were identical at the start and at the end of this audit, and the only untracked paths are the three 26.3 report files.

findings.description: Genuinely closed, and the previous friction/false-failure direction is gone. `role_mix` is now computed as `reduce (($inv + $pr)[])` (scripts/check-agents.sh:420) over the union of the task-record invocations and the phase record's own phase-reviewer entries, so it sums to `subagent_invocations_total` by construction and matches the phase-20 worked example. I verified this against both in-repo precedents: with AGGREGATE_APPLIES_FROM_PHASE lowered to 20, the immutable phase-20 record now reconciles on EVERY field including role_mix {"implementation-worker":4,"implementation-reviewer":4,"test-quality-reviewer":3,"phase-reviewer":2}, and the 26.1-amended phase-21 record (zero phase-reviewer entries, role_mix summing to 56) also reconciles - the section reports 'ok: phase aggregates reconcile with the task records' and the run exits 0. The prior defect (a defensible record following the phase-20 convention being rejected on role_mix alone) can no longer occur. The union basis is also sound against divergence: if a phase-reviewer entry is planted inside a task record while the phase record is left unchanged, the recomputation flags 9 mismatches including the doubled subagent_invocations_total and role_mix, i.e. no silent false pass in that direction. The basis is now stated in the guard comment (lines 329-332) and, per the previous recommendation, in docs/agent-contracts.md's from-phase-26 bullet ('sums recomputed from all recorded invocations (task-level plus the phase record's own)'), so a record author can no longer reasonably adopt the other convention.
evidence: sed -i 's/^AGGREGATE_APPLIES_FROM_PHASE=26$/=20/' on the copy -> 'ok: phase aggregates reconcile with the task records', 'check-agents: PASS' exit 0 (both phase 20 and 21 reconcile; grep for 'phase (20|21) aggregate' found no FAIL line).

Sensitivity of that PASS, in the previously untested in-scope direction: deleting aggregate.role_mix."phase-reviewer" from the phase-20 record -> 'FAIL: phase 20 aggregate does not reconcile with the task records: role_mix: recorded {"implementation-worker":4,"implementation-reviewer":4,"test-quality-reviewer":3} != recomputed {..., "phase-reviewer":2}'. Incrementing phase-21's role_mix."implementation-worker" -> 'FAIL: phase 21 ... role_mix: recorded {"implementation-worker":20,...} != recomputed {"implementation-worker":19,...}'. Both records restored with `cmp`.

Positive control at 26: an independently built conforming phase-26 record whose role_mix includes phase-reviewer: 2 PASSes; deleting only the role_mix."phase-reviewer" key -> 'FAIL: phase 26 aggregate does not reconcile ... role_mix: recorded {"implementation-worker":2,"implementation-reviewer":2} != recomputed {..., "phase-reviewer":2}'. My record was built independently from the on-disk 26.1/26.2 task records (4 invocations, cost 0.116799336, tokens 9009681, duration 2039, roles worker/worker/reviewer/reviewer - recomputed with jq, matching the worker's figures) and deliberately uses a DIFFERENT shape from the worker's (2 phase-reviewer entries, not 1; different token/duration/cost values), so the guard is not overfit to the worker's construction.

Divergence probe: adding a phase-reviewer entry to task record 26.1 with the phase record unchanged -> 9 mismatches incl. 'subagent_invocations_total: recorded 6 != recomputed 7' and role_mix 'phase-reviewer: 2 != 3'; 26.1 restored with `cmp`.

findings.description: The specific defect is genuinely closed. The previously undetectable case - a phase >= 26 record with a phase-review file on disk, zero phase-reviewer entries in `subagents`, and an otherwise self-consistent aggregate (attempt-1 probe R3, which PASSed) - now FAILs with a dedicated, unambiguous line. Two things are enforced where previously one was silently assumed: presence (>= 1 phase-reviewer entry when `phase-review*.json` exists) and equality (`aggregate.phase_reviewer_invocations` == the count of those entries), plus the pre-existing per-entry cost/token/duration sums. The check keys on the `phase-review*.json` glob, so an attempt-only file also triggers it; it is skipped when no phase review exists (the release-review-gate precedent, correct) and when there is no orchestration record (disclosed); and it does not crash on a non-array `subagents` (the shape check reports that first and the aggregate section still fails loudly). Residual gap, unchanged in kind and disclosed by the worker: the check enforces presence, equality and per-entry sums, not COMPLETENESS of the phase-reviewer set - see F-26.3-TQ-08.
evidence: NEG-1 (the attempt-1 undetectable PASS): phase-review.json present, both phase-reviewer entries removed from `subagents`, phase_reviewer_* zeroed, subagent_invocations_total 4, role_mix task-only, unsuffixed triple = task-level -> exit 1 with exactly one new line, 'FAIL: phase 26 has a phase review on disk but records no phase-reviewer invocation' (byte-identical to the report's recorded string).

NEG-2/NEG-2b (equality): phase_reviewer_invocations 1 vs 2 entries -> 'FAIL: phase 26 aggregate phase_reviewer_invocations is 1 but the record has 2 phase-reviewer invocation(s)' plus the aggregate mismatch line; 3 vs 2 -> '... is 3 but the record has 2 ...'. Both directions fail; the two-line output is the documented, intended consequence (interpretations[3]).
NEG-3: role_mix lacking the phase-reviewer key -> the aggregate role_mix mismatch line. Positive control: the unmodified conforming record PASSes (exit 0).
Glob robustness: renaming phase-review.json to phase-review.attempt-1.json (attempt only, zero phase-reviewer entries) still FAILs with the presence line.

No-phase-review case: a conforming record with zero phase-reviewer entries and no phase-review file PASSes (release-review gate precedent, matches the contract's 'there is no separate phase-reviewer record' clause).
Robustness: subagents set to a string -> 'FAIL: phase 26 orchestration record lacks a subagents array' plus a 9-field aggregate mismatch list; no jq crash, no silent pass.

Grandfathering preserved: the block sits inside the `[ "$p" -ge "$AGGREGATE_APPLIES_FROM_PHASE" ]` loop with the constant at 26, so phases 20-25 are untouched; and a phase-26 phase-review.json with NO orchestration.json produces no aggregate finding, exactly as the worker discloses in known_limitations[2].
findings.recommended_action: None. The contract bullet now states the requirement, so a record author cannot be rejected for a rule they were never told about.

findings.description: New (residual, expected) gap: the TQ-03 check establishes presence and equality, not completeness of the phase-reviewer set, so a record that UNDER-reports the phase-review invocations that actually occurred still passes. I demonstrated the passable-wrong-record path: a phase-26 record carrying only 1 of the 2 phase-reviewer invocations, with phase_reviewer_invocations 1 and every dependent figure made self-consistent (subagent_invocations_total 5, role_mix worker 2/reviewer 2/phase-reviewer 1, unsuffixed triple = task-level + the one entry), exits 0. This is exactly the limit the worker states in known_limitations[2] ('the guard enforces presence, equality and per-entry sums, not completeness of the set'), so it is disclosed rather than hidden; no amount of further probing of this guard could close it, since the phase record is the only authority for its own invocation list. Completeness is the phase reviewer's and the gate's responsibility, not this guard's.
evidence: RESIDUAL probe -> no FAIL line, exit 0, with 5 subagents of which 1 is phase-reviewer and role_mix summing to 5 = subagent_invocations_total.
docs/implementation/26.3/worker-report.attempt-2.json known_limitations[2] discloses precisely this limit and the no-orchestration-record case.
findings.recommended_action: None for test quality. Keep the disclosure wording; no guard change is proposed for this.

findings.description: New, pre-existing in shape (it comes from attempt 1's B3 self-check pair, not from the attempt-2 rework): the scope self-checks match the contract with a bare `grep -q "from phase $CONSTANT"`, so they can only fail when the phrase is ABSENT, not when the constant disagrees. Lowering AGGREGATE_APPLIES_FROM_PHASE from 26 to 20 leaves the contract text unchanged and the self-check still reports ok, because the contract contains 'from phase 20' for two unrelated rules - the aggregate scope drift check silently passes. The attempt-1 audit verified only the upward direction (removing the 'from phase 26' marker produced the expected FAIL), so this direction was never probed until now. Impact is bounded and in the safe direction: the undetected drift (a constant lowered, or one whose number coincides with another bullet's phrase) makes the script enforce MORE than the contract states, which surfaces as loud failures on immutable history rather than as a silent pass; and the more dangerous direction (a constant raised to a phase with no matching phrase) is still caught. Two constants are affected equally, including the pre-existing APPLIES_FROM_PHASE=20 check.
evidence: sed -i on the copy's constant only: `AGGREGATE_APPLIES_FROM_PHASE=20` -> run exits 0 with 'ok: contract aggregate enforcement scope agrees with the script' unchanged, while docs/agent-contracts.md still says 'from phase 26'. Script restored with `cmp`.
scripts/check-agents.sh:242-250 - both checks are plain `grep -q "from phase $CONSTANT"` against the whole contract, not against the specific bullet.
Attempt-1 evidence F-26.3-TQ-06 covers the upward direction only ('from phase twenty-six' -> FAIL).
findings.recommended_action: Optional hardening, not required for this task: anchor each scope grep to its own bullet (for example match the bolded '**from phase N**' marker adjacent to the rule's text) so a constant change that collides with another bullet's phrase cannot pass. No behavioural risk to the shipped configuration as it stands.

summary: All three findings from attempt 1 are genuinely closed, and I closed them by reproduction rather than by reading the report. TQ-01: the all-phases reviewer-report listing rule is restored as a separate ungated section whose logic and error line are byte-identical to the pre-change HEAD script - de-listing 15.1's reviewer report FAILs with exactly the pre-change line while the from-phase-20 evidence section still reports ok, proving the two sections run independently; the 20.1 attempt/base-kind stimuli still FAIL unlisted and PASS once listed, so nothing was weakened to achieve the restoration; the contract's '**all phases**' bullet is once again true of what the script enforces. TQ-02: role_mix is recomputed over the union of task-record invocations and the phase record's own phase-reviewer entries; with the constant lowered to 20 the immutable phase-20 record reconciles on every field including role_mix with phase-reviewer: 2, and the 26.1-amended phase-21 record reconciles too, while perturbing either phase's role_mix fails - so the previously demonstrated false-failure direction is gone and the check discriminates. I also confirmed the union basis is sound under divergence (a phase-reviewer entry planted in a task record produces nine loud mismatches, never a silent pass) and that the basis is now stated in both the guard comment and the contract, which was the previous recommendation. TQ-03: the attempt-1 undetectable PASS (phase-review file on disk, zero phase-reviewer entries, otherwise self-consistent aggregate) now FAILs with one dedicated line; unequal phase_reviewer_invocations fails in both directions; the glob also catches an attempt-only phase review; a conforming record with no phase review on disk still passes (the release-review-gate precedent); a non-array subagents fails loudly instead of crashing. Positive controls hold throughout: a correctly listed attempt passes, and an independently built conforming phase-26 record - deliberately a different shape from the worker's, with two phase-reviewer entries - passes. Two new findings, neither blocking: F-26.3-TQ-09 (LOW, inherited from attempt 1) - the scope self-checks are bare phrase greps, so lowering AGGREGATE_APPLIES_FROM_PHASE to 20 passes the drift check because the contract contains 'from phase 20' for other rules; the undetected drift only makes enforcement stricter, never a silent pass, and the risky direction is still caught; optional hardening would anchor the grep to its own bullet. F-26.3-TQ-10 (INFORMATIONAL) - docs/agent-contracts.md is now exactly at its 220-line budget, so it passes today with zero headroom. F-26.3-TQ-08 records the one residual, inherent limit: the phase-reviewer check enforces presence, equality and per-entry sums but not completeness of the set, so a record recording 1 of 2 phase-reviewer invocations still passes - which is exactly what the worker discloses in known_limitations[2], so it is honest rather than hidden. On honesty: the report's PASS claims were verified on the clean copy with docs/implementation/26.3 set aside (check-agents 15/15 ok exit 0; check-docs 9/9 ok exit 0), and the real tree's failure is exactly the disclosed three-line transient plus check-docs section 9 - so the report is careful to scope its PASS to the clean copy and does not claim the in-progress tree passes. Every mutation I made lived on the /tmp copy and was restored with `cmp`; the real tree is byte-identical at start and end apart from the three intended modified files and the untracked docs/implementation/26.3/ reports, and no phase-26 fixture was ever created there. No BLOCKER or HIGH remains, so APPROVED; the only follow-up worth doing is re-running the guard once the real phase-26 orchestration record exists, since that is the first real exercise of the phase-26 branch.
